subject.title: fix(browser): prove post-action target continuity before adopting a tab

question: Should extension-relay formally expose nonce-scoped opaque relay target handles as the CDP identity contract, replacing renderer/raw target IDs for existing relay clients?
rationale: The implementation fixes a real wrong-target boundary, but choosing the durable public identifier and its compatibility expectations is a browser-owner product/API decision rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Approve opaque relay handles with production proof
options.body: Adopt nonce-scoped per-binding handles, require the real paired-extension transcript, and document the replacement identity as the supported relay contract.

options.title: Keep raw target compatibility temporarily
options.body: Preserve or explicitly migrate the current raw-ID behavior before switching public relay identities, accepting additional compatibility complexity.

options.title: Split relay identity from route safety
options.body: Land only the backend-owned route outcome work and defer the relay public-ID migration to a separately approved browser-contract change.

recommendation.title: Approve opaque relay handles with production proof
recommendation.body: Adopt nonce-scoped per-binding handles, require the real paired-extension transcript, and document the replacement identity as the supported relay contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The canonical report defines the relay identity lifecycle and the PR discussion specifically requests this contract decision from them.
